recognize_zh: 散在數顆較小、緻密且沒有中央淡染區的紅血球，表面有數量不等、長短不一且分布不規則的尖刺或棒狀突起，與周圍正常圓盤狀紅血球形成對比，符合棘紅血球（acanthocytes／spur cells）。
features: Scattered small dense red cells lacking central pallor
Irregular, unevenly spaced projections of variable length with pointed or club-shaped tips
Background red cells largely normocytic with central pallor
No schistocytes, target cell predominance or red cell inclusions evident
No leukocytes in field; few platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a background of normocytic red cells with scattered acanthocytes. These cells are small, dense and lack central pallor, bearing a few irregularly distributed spicules of varying length, some with knob-like ends. Fragmented red cells are not prominent. Findings are consistent with acanthocytosis, as can be seen in advanced liver disease (spur cell anemia).

ddx.vs: Echinocytes have 10-30 short, evenly spaced, uniform projections and often retain central pallor, whereas acanthocytes have fewer irregular spicules and are dense.
Schistocytes have straight cut edges and sharp angular points from mechanical fragmentation rather than a round body with multiple irregular spicules.
Keratocytes have one or two horn-like projections flanking a ruptured vacuole, not multiple scattered spicules.
